provenance_note: The reference corpus was authored independently without access to the tool code; this run recomputes every check from the shipping build against the stored reference values.
reference: Hand-built daily noise-exposure shifts (single task, equal levels, time halving, short high-level burst, order permutations, Te < / > T0, 24 h boundary, user T0) with LEX,8h, LAeq,Te, EA and energy shares computed by an own 60-digit Decimal evaluation of the energy-sum definition and cross-checked by a float partial-exposure form; EU Directive 2003/10/EC threshold states on both sides of 80/85/87 dB(A) including equality; hearing-protector scenarios (user attenuation, SNR with LCeq, simplified SNR on LAeq, HML both branches incl. two published worked examples, 4 dB derating, part-time wear energy mix) with action values compared against the unprotected and the limit against the at-ear exposure (Art. 3(2)); user criteria packs; uncertainty review; invalid and insufficient inputs; 24 seeded random shifts (ref.py).
reference_citations: Directive 2003/10/EC of 6 February 2003 (noise), EUR-Lex CELEX 32003L0010, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32003L0010 — Art. 2 (LEX,8h, nominal eight-hour day), Art. 3(1) (87/85/80 dB(A)), Art. 3(2) (protectors for limit only), Art. 5-7 ('exceeded')

HSE L108 'Controlling noise at work', Control of Noise at Work Regulations 2005 guidance, https://www.hse.gov.uk/pubns/priced/l108.pdf — Schedule 1 Part 1 (p.30): LEP,d = LAeq,Te + 10 lg(Te/T0), T0 = 28 800 s, and LEP,d = 10 lg[(1/T0) sum Ti 10^(0.1 LAeq,Ti)]
ISO 9612:2009 preview, https://cdn.standards.iteh.ai/samples/41718/ab45a73ad46f45cba775b5cb4b859a2c/ISO-9612-2009.pdf — eq. (2) LEX,8h = LAeq,Te + 10 lg(Te/T0), T0 = 8 h
ISO 4869-2:2018 preview, https://cdn.standards.iteh.ai/samples/65582/cc46f40f2f0c47ac9625316046418ec1/ISO-4869-2-2018.pdf — def. 3.8 (SNR subtracted from LC)

HSE L108 Appendix 1 real-world 4 dB derating and SNR formula L'A = LC - SNR, as reproduced by Hear4TheLongTerm, https://www.hear4thelongterm.co.uk/library/2.1.1-l108-guidance-on-real-world-protection-&-de-rating-(appendix-1)

HML PNR formula for LC-LA <= 2 dB and worked example H35/M25/L20, LA 108.7, LC 109.0 -> PNR 29.3, L'A 79.4: IMO noise-code guidance as published at https://imorules.com/GUID-223C2E09-5401-4D4E-8612-B0AF276552F6.html

HML PNR formulas for both branches (LC-LA > 2 dB: PNR = M - 0.125(M-L)(LC-LA-2)) and worked example H25/M18/L13, LC 103, LA 104 -> PNR 23.3: Essel Acoustics, https://esselacoustics.com/news/the-hml-of-a-hearing-protector-using-it-to-predict-hearing-protection-performance/
Spec specs/06.md (MVP scope, QA tests, acceptance criteria); own reference bench/noiseexposure/ref.py
tolerance: Levels: absolute 1e-6 dB. A level is logarithmic, so an absolute bound on dB is a relative bound (2.3e-7) on energy and holds at every scale; the model is closed-form arithmetic with no discretisation, so only floating-point error (<1e-9 dB between the two reference forms) is expected and 1e-6 dB leaves margin for display-independent round-off while being five orders below the 0.1 dB at which thresholds are compared. Energy shares: absolute 1e-6 (dimensionless fraction). EA and durations: relative 1e-6 / 1e-9. Categorical threshold, flag and refusal outcomes: exact. Random cases whose LEX lies within 0.05 dB of a threshold carry no threshold check, so display rounding cannot decide them.

not_benchmarked.Rounding band: Threshold behaviour inside the 0.1 dB rounding band (e.g. 80.04 dB): the Directive does not prescribe a rounding convention, so no independent expectation exists.
not_benchmarked.Peak sound pressure: Peak sound pressure (Art. 3 ppeak 200/140/112 Pa): the tool does not assess it (spec: requires separate inputs).
not_benchmarked.Weekly, octave band, CSV import: Weekly exposure, octave-band method, CSV import (post-MVP).
not_benchmarked.Over-protection: EN 458 over-protection (L108 para 83: aim for 70-80 dB(A) at ear) - not a claimed tool feature.
not_benchmarked.Level and T0 upper bounds: Upper bounds on level (150 dB) and T0 (24 h): tool heuristics without a published basis.
not_benchmarked.Exports and rendering: Exports (PDF/CSV/JSON/Python), record import, locale formatting, timeline/chart rendering: not numerical claims answerable by an external reference.
not_benchmarked.Random case count: The spec's 100-random-case QA target: the corpus carries 24 random shifts to stay within the 25-80 case budget of the benchmark brief.

domain_self_tests.note: 68 of 68 built-in self-tests pass over 22 rule IDs.

adapter.note: Every case runs evaluate(), the function behind the interface; user attenuation with derating is entered as the net effective attenuation (noted per case).

python_export.note: The exported standard-library script reproduces the displayed outputs within 1e-9 relative.
